koryo-saram.name: Koryo-saram
koryo-saram.summary: Ethnic Koreans of the former Soviet Union descended from settlers in the Russian Far East from the late 19th century; deported to Central Asia in 1937, with about 500,000 living across former Soviet states today.

morkovcha.name: Morkovcha
morkovcha.summary: A spicy marinated carrot salad from Koryo-saram cuisine, the food of ethnic Koreans of the former Soviet Union.

pilaf.name: Pilaf
pilaf.summary: A rice or wheat dish cooked in stock with spices and other ingredients, spread widely from the Abbasid Caliphate and known regionally as pilov, polow, pulao or paella.

nikita-khrushchev.name: Nikita Khrushchev
nikita-khrushchev.summary: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964 who denounced Stalin's rule, launched de-Stalinization, and led the country through the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis.

virgin-lands-campaign.name: Virgin Lands campaign
virgin-lands-campaign.summary: Nikita Khrushchev's 1953 plan sending hundreds of thousands of volunteers to farm the steppe of Kazakhstan and Siberia to boost Soviet grain output; it later caused severe soil erosion.

komsomol.name: Komsomol
komsomol.summary: The Soviet Union's communist youth organization, established in 1918, for members up to age 28 who had graduated from the Young Pioneers.

teahouse.name: Chaikhana
teahouse.summary: An establishment serving tea and light refreshments that often functions as a center of social interaction, much like a coffee house.

beshbarmak.name: Beshbarmak
beshbarmak.summary: Traditional Central Asian dish of boiled meat, noodles and onion broth, whose name means "five fingers" for the practice of eating it by hand.

piy-la.name: Piyāla
piy-la.summary: A small handleless ceramic bowl used across Central Asia for drinking tea, also called piala or chini, designed to stack easily for nomadic use.

dungan-people.name: Dungan people
dungan-people.summary: Muslims of Hui origin living in the former Soviet Union, found today mainly in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Russia.

hui-people.name: Hui people
hui-people.summary: A Chinese-speaking Muslim ethnic group found mainly in northwestern China, numbering about 11.3 million according to the 2020 census.

qatiq.name: Qatiq
qatiq.summary: A thick fermented milk product from Turkic countries and Bulgaria, made by fermenting boiled milk for 6 to 10 hours, firmer than ordinary yogurt.

kumis.name: Kumis
kumis.summary: Traditional fermented drink made from mare's milk, central to Turkic and Mongolic peoples of the Central and East Asian steppes, also called airag, with a higher alcohol content than kefir.

ayran.name: Ayran
ayran.summary: A cold, salted yogurt drink consumed by Turkic peoples for about 1,000 years, and today the national drink of Turkey.

mongol-zurag.name: Mongol zurag
mongol-zurag.summary: A style of Mongolian painting begun in the early 20th century, using mineral paint on cotton to show secular, nationalist scenes, distinct from Buddhist art and Soviet socialist realism.

ashgabat.name: Ashgabat
ashgabat.summary: The capital and largest city of Turkmenistan, founded in 1881 and rebuilt with white marble monuments after a devastating 1948 earthquake.

russian-avant-garde.name: Russian avant-garde
russian-avant-garde.summary: An influential wave of modern art movements in the Russian Empire and Soviet Union from about 1890 to 1930, including Suprematism, Constructivism and Futurism, before clashing with state-imposed Socialist Realism.

marzan-sharav.name: Balduugiin Sharav
marzan-sharav.summary: Mongolian painter (1869–1939) often credited with introducing modern painting styles to Mongolia, best known for his work 'One Day in Mongolia'.

dushanbe.name: Dushanbe
dushanbe.summary: Capital and largest city of Tajikistan, known as Stalinabad from 1929 to 1961 after Joseph Stalin, settled by various ancient empires before growing into a modern city.

palace-of-the-nation-dushanbe.name: Palace of the Nation, Dushanbe
palace-of-the-nation-dushanbe.summary: The official residence of the President of Tajikistan in the capital, Dushanbe, built by an Italian construction company.

rjingiin-yadams-ren.name: Ürjingiin Yadamsüren
rjingiin-yadams-ren.summary: A Mongolian artist, 1905 to 1987, best known for popularising the Mongol zurag style of painting.

secret-history-of-the-mongols.name: Secret History of the Mongols
secret-history-of-the-mongols.summary: The oldest surviving literary work in Mongolic languages, written for the Mongol royal family after Genghis Khan's death in 1227 to recount his life, conquests, and part of his successor's reign.

genghis-khan.name: Genghis Khan
genghis-khan.summary: Founder of the Mongol Empire (c. 1162-1227), who united the Mongol tribes and conquered large parts of China and Central Asia.

national-library-of-tajikistan.name: National Library of Tajikistan
national-library-of-tajikistan.summary: Main library of Tajikistan in Dushanbe, tracing back to a 1933 library and reopened in a new nine-story building in 2012 with 15 reading halls, free to any Tajik citizen.

tajikistan-national-museum.name: National Museum of Tajikistan
tajikistan-national-museum.summary: A museum in Dushanbe, the capital city of Tajikistan.

saparmurat-niyazov.name: Saparmurat Niyazov
saparmurat-niyazov.summary: Turkmen dictator (1940–2006) who led Turkmenistan from 1985 until his death, ruled as president for life from 1999, and built an eccentric personality cult around his book the Ruhnama.

neutrality-monument.name: Monument of Neutrality
neutrality-monument.summary: A 75-metre monument and observation tower built in Ashgabat, Turkmenistan in 1998 to mark the country's official neutrality, originally topped by a rotating gold statue of President Niyazov.

ashgabat-international-airport.name: Ashgabat International Airport
ashgabat-international-airport.summary: One of Turkmenistan's international airports, located in the capital Ashgabat, with a terminal redesigned and reopened in 2016.

basmachi-movement.name: Basmachi movement
basmachi-movement.summary: An uprising against Russian imperial and then Soviet rule in Central Asia, rooted in 1916 anti-conscription violence and a 1918 massacre in Kokand, fighting to defend the local way of life.

russian-turkestan.name: Russian Turkestan
russian-turkestan.summary: A vast Central Asian region governed by the Russian Empire from 1867, often called a colonial possession, populated mainly by Uzbek, Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Tajik speakers.

manchukuo.name: Manchukuo
manchukuo.summary: A Japanese puppet state set up in Manchuria in 1932, nominally ruled by former Chinese emperor Puyi but with all real decisions made by Japanese officials, lasting until 1945.

joseph-stalin.name: Joseph Stalin
joseph-stalin.summary: Soviet politician who ruled the Soviet Union from 1922 until his death in 1953, becoming its de facto dictator by the 1930s and formalizing Marxism–Leninism.

kalmyks.name: Kalmyks
kalmyks.summary: A Mongolic people in Europe descended from Oirats who migrated from Dzungaria in early modern times and founded the Kalmyk Khanate in the 17th century; Europe's only traditionally Buddhist ethnic group.

cossacks.name: Cossacks
cossacks.summary: An East Slavic, Eastern Orthodox militant people from the Pontic-Caspian steppe who defended borders of Poland-Lithuania and Russia in exchange for self-governing autonomy.

tashkent-soviet.name: Tashkent Soviet
tashkent-soviet.summary: A public organization formed by railway workers in Tashkent during the 1917 Russian Revolution, which came to be made up entirely of Bolshevik soldiers and workers.

jadid.name: Jadid movement
jadid.summary: A Turco-Islamic modernist movement in the late 19th- and early 20th-century Russian Empire that promoted Islamic reform, new-method schooling, and print media.

kokand.name: Kokand
kokand.summary: A city in eastern Uzbekistan's Fergana Valley, a historic crossroads of trade routes, whose Jadid government briefly declared Turkestan's autonomy in 1917 before being crushed by Soviet forces.

tajikistani-civil-war.name: Tajik Civil War
tajikistani-civil-war.summary: An armed conflict in Tajikistan from 1992 to 1997 between the government and an opposition coalition, backed by Russian forces on the government side; it killed tens of thousands and displaced much of the population.

islamic-renaissance-party-of-tajikistan.name: Islamic Renaissance Party
islamic-renaissance-party-of-tajikistan.summary: A banned Islamist political party in Tajikistan, the only legal Islamist party in Central Asia until it was designated a terrorist organisation in 2015.

khorloogiin-choibalsan.name: Khorloogiin Choibalsan
khorloogiin-choibalsan.summary: Mongolian revolutionary and premier of the Mongolian People's Republic from 1939 to 1952, commander-in-chief of its army from 1937, who ran a repressive Stalinist dictatorship with purges from 1937 to 1939.

oirats.name: Oirats
oirats.summary: The westernmost group of Mongols, originally from the Altai region of Siberia, Xinjiang and western Mongolia; today's Kalmyks of southeastern Europe descend from them.

zemchin-mongols.name: Üzemchin
zemchin-mongols.summary: A subgroup of Mongols living in eastern Mongolia and Inner Mongolia, whose name likely comes from a word meaning grape pickers.

inner-mongolian-army.name: Inner Mongolian Army
inner-mongolian-army.summary: A mostly cavalry force of ethnic Mongols serving Imperial Japan and its puppet state Mengjiang during the Second Sino-Japanese War, led chiefly by Prince Demchugdongrub.

mengjiang.name: Mengjiang
mengjiang.summary: A Japanese-backed puppet state established in 1939 in Inner Mongolia, covering former Chinese provinces, which returned to Chinese control after Japan's 1945 defeat.

tsendiin-damdins-ren.name: Tsendiin Damdinsüren
tsendiin-damdins-ren.summary: Mongolian writer and linguist (1908–1986) who wrote the lyrics to one version of Mongolia's national anthem.

chagatai-language.name: Chagatai language
chagatai-language.summary: A now-extinct Turkic literary language once widely spoken across Central Asia until the early 20th century, and the direct ancestor of modern Uzbek and Uyghur.

mongol-internationale.name: Mongol Internationale
mongol-internationale.summary: The first national anthem of the Mongolian People's Republic, used from 1924 to 1950.

vladimir-lenin.name: Vladimir Lenin
vladimir-lenin.summary: Russian revolutionary and political theorist (1870–1924) who led the Bolsheviks and became the first head of government of Soviet Russia, then the Soviet Union, developing Marxism into Leninism.

damdin-s-khbaatar.name: Damdin Sükhbaatar
damdin-s-khbaatar.summary: A Mongolian revolutionary (1893–1923) who founded the Mongolian People's Party and led the partisan army that took Khüree in the 1921 Mongolian Revolution, honored as 'Father of Mongolia's Revolution.'

naskh-script.name: Naskh script
naskh-script.summary: A small, round style of Islamic calligraphy, among the earliest to develop, widely used for administrative documents and for copying books, including the Qur'an, for its legibility.

sputnik-1.name: Sputnik 1
sputnik-1.summary: The first artificial Earth satellite, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957, whose unexpected success triggered the Space Race.

baikonur-cosmodrome.name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
baikonur-cosmodrome.summary: A spaceport in Kazakhstan operated by Russia, founded in 1955 as the Soviet Union's chief space base; it launched Sputnik 1 and Yuri Gagarin's first crewed spaceflight.

yuri-gagarin.name: Yuri Gagarin
yuri-gagarin.summary: Soviet cosmonaut (1934–1968) who became the first person in space, orbiting Earth aboard Vostok 1 in 1961.

vostok-1.name: Vostok 1
vostok-1.summary: The first human orbital spaceflight, launched on 12 April 1961 with Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin aboard, completing one orbit of Earth in 108 minutes.

gagarin-s-start.name: Gagarin's Start
gagarin-s-start.summary: Retired launch site at the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, used by the Soviet space program and later Roscosmos.

nurek-dam.name: Nurek Dam
nurek-dam.summary: An earth-fill embankment dam on Tajikistan's Vakhsh River, whose power station has an installed capacity of 3,015 MW.

vakhsh-river.name: Vakhsh River
vakhsh-river.summary: A river in Central Asia and one of the main rivers of Tajikistan, a tributary of the Amu Darya.

aral-sea.name: Aral Sea
aral-sea.summary: A former salt lake between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, once the world's third-largest lake, whose name means "Sea of Islands" for its more than 1,100 islands.

valentina-tereshkova.name: Valentina Tereshkova
valentina-tereshkova.summary: Soviet cosmonaut born in 1937 who became the first woman in space in 1963, later serving decades in Soviet and Russian politics.

dike-kokaral.name: Dike Kokaral
dike-kokaral.summary: 12-kilometre dam completed in 2005 with World Bank help, splitting the shrinking Aral Sea to preserve the North Aral Sea at the expense of the larger southern part.

lake-balkhash.name: Lake Balkhash
lake-balkhash.summary: A large lake in southeastern Kazakhstan, one of the biggest in Asia, with a fresh western half and a saline eastern half.

r-16-missile.name: R-16
r-16-missile.summary: The Soviet Union's first successful intercontinental ballistic missile, known in the West by the NATO name SS-7 Saddler.

angara-rocket-family.name: Angara (rocket family)
angara-rocket-family.summary: A family of Russian launch vehicles developed by the Khrunichev State Research and Production Space Center, able to carry between 3,800 and 24,500 kg into low Earth orbit, intended to replace several older rockets.

borjigin.name: Borjigin
borjigin.summary: A Mongol clan founded in the early 10th century by Bodonchar Munkhag whose senior line supplied Mongolia's ruling princes and formed the Mongols' ruling class into the 20th century.

bogd-khanate-of-mongolia.name: Bogd Khanate of Mongolia
bogd-khanate-of-mongolia.summary: A Mongolian state existing 1911 to 1919 and 1921 to 1924, formed after the Qing dynasty's collapse and ruled by the Bogd Khaan, combining religious and political authority.

central-asian-revolt-of-1916.name: Central Asian revolt of 1916
central-asian-revolt-of-1916.summary: An anti-Russian uprising by indigenous Turkestani peoples sparked by wartime conscription of Muslims, whose suppression by Russian forces caused an estimated 100,000 to 500,000 deaths.

turkestan.name: Turkestan
turkestan.summary: A historical Central Asian region between the Caspian Sea, Siberia, the Gobi Desert and the Indian subcontinent, mainly Turkic-inhabited, split into former Russian West Turkestan and Chinese East Turkestan.

uzbek-soviet-socialist-republic.name: Uzbek SSR
uzbek-soviet-socialist-republic.summary: A union republic of the Soviet Union governed by its Communist Party from 1925 until 1991, when it declared independence as Uzbekistan.

turkmen-soviet-socialist-republic.name: Turkmen SSR
turkmen-soviet-socialist-republic.summary: A constituent republic of the Soviet Union in Central Asia from 1925 to 1991, bordered by Iran, Afghanistan and the Caspian Sea, which became independent Turkmenistan in 1991.

tajik-soviet-socialist-republic.name: Tajik SSR
tajik-soviet-socialist-republic.summary: A constituent republic of the Soviet Union in Central Asia from 1929 to 1991, later becoming independent Tajikistan.

kara-kirghiz-autonomous-oblast.name: Kara-Kirghiz Autonomous Oblast
kara-kirghiz-autonomous-oblast.summary: A Soviet region created in 1924 from the Kyrgyz part of Turkestan, renamed in 1925, then reorganized into the Kirghiz ASSR in 1926 and the Kirghiz SSR by 1936.

khanate-of-khiva.name: Khanate of Khiva
khanate-of-khiva.summary: An Uzbek monarchy centered on the city of Khiva in the Khorezm oasis, ruling from 1511 to 1920 (with a mid-1700s interruption) before becoming a Russian protectorate and later Soviet territory.

navaanneren.name: Navaanneren Setsen Khan
navaanneren.summary: 20th Khan of the hereditary Setsen Khanate in eastern Mongolia, a line descending from Genghis Khan; he lived from 1877 to 1937.

chinggisids.name: Chinggisids
chinggisids.summary: The descendants of Genghis Khan and his wife Börte, who by tradition were considered the only legitimate rulers of the Mongol Empire and its successor states, a rule that lasted until 1847.

anandyn-amar.name: Anandyn Amar
anandyn-amar.summary: Head of state of the Mongolian People's Republic from 1932 to 1936 and twice prime minister, known for defending Mongolian independence against Soviet domination before being purged and executed in 1941.

mongolian-people-s-republic.name: Mongolian People's Republic
mongolian-people-s-republic.summary: Mongolia's communist state from 1924 to 1992, the world's second communist country and the Soviet Union's first and longest-lasting satellite state.

tengrism.name: Tengrism
tengrism.summary: A belief system from the Eurasian steppes based on shamanism and animism and centered on the sky god Tengri, once the state religion of several medieval Turkic and Mongol states.

tengri.name: Tengri
tengri.summary: The sky god of traditional Turkic and Mongolic beliefs, seen as eternal, supreme, and the judge and source of life; worship centered on him is called Tengrism.

dastan-sarygulov.name: Dastan Sarygulov
dastan-sarygulov.summary: Kyrgyz businessman and politician, born 1947, who headed the state gold company Kyrgyzaltyn from 1992 to 1999. He was arrested in 2016 on suspicion of plotting to seize power.

ismailism.name: Ismailism
ismailism.summary: A denomination of Shia Islam, one of three alongside Twelver and Zaydi Islam, marked by its distinctive emphasis on the esoteric, hidden meaning of Islamic teaching.

pamir-mountains.name: Pamir Mountains
pamir-mountains.summary: A mountain range in Central and South Asia where the Tian Shan, Karakoram, Kunlun, Hindu Kush and Himalayas meet, known since Victorian times as the 'Roof of the World.'

twelver-shi-ism.name: Twelver Shi'ism
twelver-shi-ism.summary: The largest branch of Shia Islam, holding that twelve divinely appointed Imams beginning with Ali succeeded the prophet Muhammad, with the twelfth expected to return as the Mahdi.

samarkand.name: Samarkand
samarkand.summary: A major city in southeastern Uzbekistan and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Central Asia, a key Silk Road center once capital of the Achaemenid satrapy of Sogdiana.

bukhara.name: Bukhara
bukhara.summary: Ancient Silk Road city in what is now Uzbekistan, a major center of Islamic scholarship and birthplace of Imam Bukhari, later capital of the Emirate of Bukhara until 1920.

stalinist-repressions-in-mongolia.name: Great Repression
stalinist-repressions-in-mongolia.summary: Period of political violence in the Mongolian People's Republic from 1937 to 1939, an extension of Stalin's purges. Between 20,000 and 35,000 people were executed, with Buddhist clergy among those hit hardest.

9th-jebtsundamba-khutughtu.name: 9th Jebtsundamba Khutughtu
9th-jebtsundamba-khutughtu.summary: Mongolian Buddhist leader (1933–2012) and spiritual head of the Gelug lineage among the Khalkha Mongols. He was recognized as the Bogd Khan's reincarnation in 1936, and he did not live in Mongolia until the last year of his life.

bogd-khan.name: Bogd Khan
bogd-khan.summary: Born in Tibet, he ruled Mongolia as khan from 1911 to 1924, after it became de facto independent from Qing China. He was also the 8th Jebtsundamba Khutuktu, or "Bogdo Lama" (1869 to 1924).

gandantegchinlen-monastery.name: Gandantegchinlen Monastery
gandantegchinlen-monastery.summary: Buddhist monastery in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, founded in 1809 and closed amid persecutions in 1939. From 1944 to 1989 it was the country's only active monastery, and it is now the center of Mongolian Buddhism.

yellow-shamanism.name: Yellow shamanism
yellow-shamanism.summary: Form of shamanism practiced in Mongolia and Siberia that includes Buddhist rituals and traditions. 'Yellow' refers to the Yellow sect of Tibetan Buddhism, whose members wear yellow hats.

buryats.name: Buryats
buryats.summary: A Mongol ethnic group native to southeastern Siberia and northern Mongolia, traditionally regarded as the main northern branch of the Mongols and known for nomadic herding.

black-shamanism.name: Black shamanism
black-shamanism.summary: Kind of shamanism practiced in Mongolia and Siberia, set against yellow shamanism, which includes Buddhist rituals. Its practitioners are usually seen as working with evil spirits.

nganasan-people.name: Nganasan people
nganasan-people.summary: Samoyedic-speaking indigenous people of the Taymyr Peninsula in north Siberia. They were traditionally semi-nomadic wild reindeer hunters, taxed under Tsarist Russia from the early 17th century and settled in villages in the 1970s.

pan-mongolism.name: Pan-Mongolism
pan-mongolism.summary: A 20th-century nationalist idea calling for the unity of all Mongols, from Mongolia to Inner Mongolia and Buryatia, into a 'Greater Mongolia'.

khalkha-mongols.name: Khalkha Mongols
khalkha-mongols.summary: The largest subgroup of the Mongols in present-day Mongolia since the 15th century, historically ruled directly by Borjigin khans and making up most of Mongolia's population today.

khangai-mountains.name: Khangai Mountains
khangai-mountains.summary: A mountain range in central Mongolia, about 400 km west of the capital Ulaanbaatar.

aktau.name: Aktau
aktau.summary: A major port city in southwestern Kazakhstan on the Caspian Sea's eastern shore, on the Mangyshlak Peninsula; from 1964 to 1991 it was named Shevchenko.

taras-shevchenko.name: Taras Shevchenko
taras-shevchenko.summary: Ukrainian poet, writer and artist (1814–1861) whose poetry collection Kobzar is considered the foundation of modern Ukrainian literature.

tumed.name: Tümed
tumed.summary: A Mongol subgroup living mainly around Hohhot in China, descended from tribes conquered by Genghis Khan and later reaching their peak under Altan Khan in the 16th century.
